ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, point C is on $BE$, $\angle B = \angle E = \angle ACF$, $AC = CF$, $AB = 4$, and $EF = 6$. What is the length of $BE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle B+\angle BAC=\angle ACE=\angle FCE+\angle ACF$,\\
and since $\angle B=\angle ACF$,\\
it follows that $\angle BAC=\angle FCE$,\\
Since $\angle B=\angle E$, $AC=CF$,\\
it follows that $\triangle ABC\cong \triangle CEF$,\\
therefore $AB=CE$, $BC=EF$,\\
Since $AB=4$, $EF=6$,\\
it follows that $BE=BC+CE=6+4=\boxed{10}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached diagram, B, C, and E lie on one straight horizontal line, with C between B and E. Point A is above the left part of the base, point F is above C, and the drawn segments form triangles ABC and CEF, with ray CF lying inside angle ACE. Reasoning: Let the common given angle be ∠B = ∠E = ∠ACF. Since B, C, and E are collinear, ∠ACE is an exterior angle of triangle ABC, so ∠ACE = ∠B + ∠BAC. Also, from the diagram CF splits ∠ACE, so ∠ACE = ∠ACF + ∠FCE. Because ∠B = ∠ACF, subtracting equal angles gives ∠BAC = ∠FCE. Now compare triangles ABC and CEF: ∠ABC = ∠CEF, ∠BAC = ∠FCE, and AC = CF. Therefore triangle ABC is congruent to triangle CEF by AAS, with correspondence A↔C, B↔E, C↔F. Hence CE = AB = 4 and BC = EF = 6. Since C lies between B and E, BE = BC + CE = 6 + 4 = 10.
